title: Case study: Did the fund beat the market?

questions.prompt: A fund calls 50 from investors in year 1 and 50 in year 2. It pays out 30 in year 4, 60 in year 6 and 90 in year 8. What is its TVPI, total paid out over total paid in? Answer to two decimals.
questions.explanation: TVPI = (30 + 60 + 90) / (50 + 50) = 180 / 100 = 1.80. Like the IRR, it says nothing about what the stock market did over the same years.

questions.prompt: Investors pay 100 into a fund at the end of year 1 and get 200 back at the end of year 10. Over the same years, one dollar in the stock market grew to 2.5 dollars. What is the fund's PME? Answer to two decimals.
questions.explanation: The 100 paid in would have grown to 250 in the market. The payout is 200, already at the end of year 10. PME = 200 / 250 = 0.80: the fund doubled the money, but the market did better.

questions.prompt: The case's fund, started in 1990, has a PME of 0.82. What does that mean?
choices: The fund lost 18% of the money investors paid in
The fund's IRR was 18 percentage points below the market's return
Valued at the stock market's returns, the payouts were worth 82% of the pay-ins, so the same money in the market would have done better
Investors will receive another 82 per 100 committed
questions.explanation: The fund paid out 1.90 times what it took in, so investors did not lose money. Carried to 1999 at the market's returns, though, the payouts were worth 343.4 against 420.9 for the pay-ins: 82%.

questions.prompt: The same fund has a 13.28% IRR whether it starts in 1990 or in 2000, but a PME of 0.82 in one case and 1.51 in the other. Why?
choices: The fund's cash flows were larger when it started in 2000
The PME compares the fund with the stock market over the same years, and the market returned about 21% a year in the 1990s and about 1% in the 2000s
The IRR depends on the year the fund starts, but the PME does not
The PME ignores when the cash flows happen
questions.explanation: The cash flows, and so the IRR and TVPI, are identical. Only the benchmark changes: the market returned 21.01% a year from 1991 to 1999 and 0.96% a year from 2001 to 2009.

questions.prompt: The stock market returned 24.25% in 1998 and 25.23% in 1999. A payout of 40 at the end of 1997, reinvested in the market, is worth how much at the end of 1999? Answer to one decimal.
The PME divides each cash flow by the market's growth to the end of the fund. That is discounting at which rate?
choices: A weighted average cost of capital chosen in advance
The stock market's actual return in each year
questions.explanation: Each flow is moved through time at what the stock market really returned year by year. The previous case discounted at a fixed 7.57% set in advance.

questions.prompt: A buyout fund that borrowed heavily has a PME of 1.05. Which statement is the most careful?
choices: It beat the stock market with the same timing, but its equity was riskier than the market's, so a PME just above 1 may not pay enough for that risk
It beat the market by 5% a year
Because the PME is above 1, the fund was as safe as the stock market
questions.explanation: A PME of 1.05 means the payouts were worth 5% more than the pay-ins at market returns, over the whole fund, not 5% a year. The benchmark is the whole market, which is less risky than equity in companies bought with a lot of debt.
